title: Language models represent more about emphasis than they can tell you
abstract: arXiv:2611.25808v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Prosodic prominence can largely be predicted from the words of a sentence, but part of it depends on how the speaker reads it. We study how much of prominence language models recover from text, whether they can report it when asked, and what the speech signal adds. On read English speech labelled for word-level prominence, we compare frozen and fine-tuned text models, prompted large language models (LLMs) and speech models on the same words. All text models end within about one point of each other, at best 68.8% on the 3-way task, and largely make the same errors. With the prompts we tested, LLMs do no better than a word-majority baseline, even with 500 examples. Linear probes find more in their representations. Speech models reach 84.7%. We argue that text determines only part of prominence, and that the rest has to be heard. translated_title: 语言模型对重音信息的表征多于它们所能表达的
translated_abstract: 韵律突显在很大程度上可以通过句子的词语来预测，但其中一部分取决于说话人的朗读方式。我们研究了语言模型能从文本中恢复多少突显信息，在被询问时能否将其报告出来，以及语音信号能带来多少额外信息。在标注了词级突显的英语朗读语音上，我们在相同的词上比较了冻结和微调的文本模型、经提示的大语言模型（LLM）以及语音模型。所有文本模型的最终性能彼此相差约一个百分点以内，在三类任务上最好达到68.8%，并且它们在很大程度上犯同样的错误。在我们测试的提示方式下，即使给出500个示例，LLM的表现也不优于“词多数”基线。而线性探针则在其内部表示中发现了更多信息。语音模型达到84.7%。我们认为，文本只决定了突显的一部分，其余部分必须通过听觉才能获得。LLM编码了文本所能决定的内容，但提示并不能将其引出：它们对重音位置的表征……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究发现语言模型内部编码了文本所能决定的重音突显信息，但通过提示无法将其表达出来，而完整的重音信息必须依赖语音信号才能获得。
en_tdlr: Language models internally encode the text-determined part of prosodic prominence but cannot report it when prompted, and the remaining part of prominence must be heard from the speech signal.
